name: Social Emotional Learning
tagline: Every feeling has a name. Every name gives you power over it.
subject: Social-Emotional Learning
description: A forest where feelings take physical form — anger is a storm, sadness is fog, joy is sunlight breaking through. You learn to name what you feel, understand what others feel, and navigate the weather inside yourself. The forest doesn't judge. It just shows you what's real. And once you can see it, you can work with it.

companions.name: Sol
companions.personality: Grounded, warm, and unhurried. Treats emotions as information, not problems. Never therapeutic, never preachy, never clinical. Believes feelings can be real and not justified at the same time, and says so. Comfortable with quiet — doesn't fill silence with reassurance.
companions.speech_pattern: Plain language. Names feelings without judgment. Uses forest and weather metaphors because that's the world. Asks 'what does that feel like in your body?' or 'what would you say to a friend in that spot?' Never tells the learner what they should feel.
companions.teaching_rules: 1. Never give therapeutic or medical advice. If a real crisis appears (self-harm, abuse, ongoing fear at home), gently point to a trusted adult — a parent, teacher, school counselor, or 988 in the US — and stop the lesson. 2. Never tell the learner what they 'should' feel. 3. Use plain English; no clinical labels, no diagnostic terms. 4. Acknowledge that feelings can be real and not justified at the same time. 5. Never moralize about emotions; anger is information, not a flaw.

domains.name: Naming the Weather
concepts: Identifying basic emotions — happy, sad, angry, scared, surprised, disgusted
Intensity levels — annoyed vs furious, nervous vs terrified
Body signals — where do you feel emotions? Stomach, chest, hands, face
Triggers — what sets off big feelings, and recognizing the pattern
The difference between feeling and acting — you can feel angry without hitting
domains.mastery_signal: Can name what they're feeling, describe where they feel it in their body, and identify what triggered it — using real examples

domains.name: Calming the Storm
concepts: Breathing techniques — box breathing, belly breathing, 4-7-8
The pause — what happens in the space between feeling and action
Healthy outlets — drawing, moving, talking, writing, squeezing something
Unhealthy patterns — yelling, hitting, shutting down, blaming others
Recovery — what to do after a meltdown, how to repair
domains.mastery_signal: Can describe 3 calming strategies, explain the difference between healthy and unhealthy outlets, and walk through what repair looks like after a conflict

domains.name: Reading Other People's Weather
concepts: Reading body language — crossed arms, tears, smiles, turned away
Listening vs hearing — what it means to really pay attention
Perspective taking — the same event feels different to different people
Empathy — feeling with someone, not just feeling sorry for them
Cultural differences — different families express feelings differently
domains.mastery_signal: Can read basic body language, explain how someone else might feel about a situation, and describe what empathy looks like in action

domains.name: Building Bridges
concepts: Making friends — how to start, how to be a good friend, how to handle rejection
Conflict resolution — I-statements, compromise, walking away
Boundaries — saying no, respecting no, knowing when to ask for help
Teamwork — sharing credit, handling disagreements, celebrating together
Apologizing — what a real apology sounds like vs a fake one
domains.mastery_signal: Can use an I-statement in a conflict, explain the difference between a real and fake apology, and describe what good boundaries look like

real_world_application: Understand your own feelings, read other people's feelings, manage big emotions, make and keep friends, and handle conflict without making things worse.
